name: optional_mutations_m_terra__invert_has_value
description: Flips the has_value() observer relation so engaged optionals report false and disengaged optionals report true.

name: optional_mutations_m_terra__zero_value_absent
description: Weakens the engagement boundary by treating a stored zero int as absence even though std::optional<int>{0} is engaged.

name: optional_mutations_m_sonnet__reset_no_op
description: reset()'s postcondition is weakened from establishing 'no value' (this |-> optionalR 1$m None) to merely restating whatever state already held (this |-> optionalR 1$m state, reusing the precondition's existential). reset() becomes a state-preserving no-op in the model: calling it on an engaged optional leaves it engaged. Still compiles because the precondition/postcondition shapes remain well-typed; only the effect is lost.

name: optional_mutations_m_sonnet__emplace_no_op
description: emplace(v)'s postcondition is weakened from establishing engagement with the newly constructed value (this |-> optionalR 1$m (Some value)) to reusing the precondition's state variable (this |-> optionalR 1$m state). The model never records that emplace succeeded: a disengaged optional stays disengaged, and an already-engaged optional keeps its old value instead of the refreshed one. Kills every real client that relies on emplace's engaged post-state, whether starting disengaged, already engaged, or emplacing zero.

name: optional_mutations_m_sonnet__nullopt_assign_no_op
description: operator=(nullopt_t)'s postcondition is weakened from establishing 'no value' (this |-> optionalR 1$m None) to restating the precondition's state (this |-> optionalR 1$m state). Assigning std::nullopt to an engaged optional no longer disengages it in the model -- the single most common way real code clears an optional silently becomes a no-op.

name: optional_mutations_m_sonnet__move_ctor_disengages_source
description: Move construction is remodeled after the common but incorrect owning-pointer intuition (as with std::unique_ptr): the source's engagement fact is split out of the shared \prepost quantifier into a \pre, and the postcondition adds otherp |-> optionalR 1$m None, so the moved-from source is left disengaged instead of retaining its abstract engagement. This drops/duplicates the resource incorrectly -- the destination gains the value while the source's ownership is wrongly extinguished, contradicting the standard's requirement that only the contained int (not the engagement) is moved from.
